channel.title: Publications on Mónica Benito
channel.description: Recent content in Publications on Mónica Benito

item.title: Floquet physics from quantized light-matter interaction: geometric phases, gauge consistency, and entanglement
item.description: How Floquet physics of classically driven systems emerges from fully quantized light-matter interaction.

item.title: Modeling of flopping-mode spin qubits: Beyond the two-site model
item.description: A spatially resolved model of flopping-mode spin qubits that goes beyond the usual two-site description.

item.title: Multi-cavity strong coupling to an electron spin ensemble: spectral and dark-state signatures
item.description: Several superconducting cavities strongly coupled to one spin ensemble, with signatures of dark states.

item.title: Lindblad theory of linear response susceptibility and dispersive readout in minimal Kitaev junctions
item.description: A Lindblad-based linear response theory for readout of hybrid superconductor-semiconductor quantum dots.

item.title: Fast coherent control of a charge qubit on solid neon with a spin-qubit-compatible resonator
item.description: A charge qubit on solid neon with fast coherent control, coupled to a magnetic-field-compatible resonator.

item.title: NbTiN nanowire resonators and prospects for spin-photon coupling with electrons on solid neon
item.description: Superconducting NbTiN nanowire resonators keep their high quality on solid neon, a step toward spin qubits with electrons on neon.

item.title: Escaping AB caging via Floquet engineering: photo-induced long-range interference in an all-band-flat model
item.description: Periodic driving lets particles escape Aharonov-Bohm caging in a flat-band diamond chain.

item.title: Electrical readout of spins in the absence of spin blockade
item.description: A way to read out spins electrically even when spin blockade is lifted.

item.title: Readout of multi-level quantum geometry from electronic transport
item.description: A protocol to measure the quantum geometric tensor in tunnel and molecular junctions.

item.title: Polarimetry with Spins in the Solid State
item.description: Pauli spin blockade, the standard spin readout in semiconductor qubits, seen as polarimetry with spins.

item.title: SymPT: a comprehensive tool for automating effective Hamiltonian derivations
item.description: SymPT, a software tool that automates Schrieffer-Wolff transformations for effective Hamiltonians.

item.title: Closed-Form Generators for Perturbative Transformations in Static and Periodically Driven Quantum Systems
item.description: A closed-form expression for the generator of perturbative transformations, for static and periodically driven systems.

item.title: Unified linear response theory of quantum electronic circuits
item.description: One theory for the electrical response of quantum devices at any frequency, including relaxation and dephasing.

item.title: Ground-state phase diagram and parity-flipping microwave transitions in a gate-tunable Josephson junction
item.description: Microwave spectroscopy of a gate-tunable InAs nanowire Josephson junction reveals unexpected parity-flipping transitions.

item.title: Blueprint for quantum computing using electrons on helium
item.description: We theoretically propose a new way to realize qubits: a hybrid qubit system consisting of the quantized vertical motion (Rydberg states) and the spin states of electrons on the surface of liquid helium.

item.title: Entangling Nuclear Spins in Distant Quantum Dots via an Electron Bus
item.description: Protocol for the deterministic generation of entanglement between two ensembles of nuclear spins surrounding two distant quantum dots.

item.title: Hole-spin qubits in Ge nanowire quantum dots: Interplay of orbital magnetic field, strain, and growth direction
item.description: Hole-spin qubits in quasi-one-dimensional structures are a promising platform for quantum information processing because of the strong spin-orbit interaction (SOI). We present analytical results and discuss device designs that optimize the SOI in Ge semiconductors.

item.title: Squeezed hole spin qubits in Ge quantum dots with ultrafast gates at low power
item.description: We propose a minimal design modification of Ge planar quantum dot devices that enhances the spin-orbit interaction by orders of magnitude and enables low power ultrafast hole-spin qubit operations.

item.title: Programable two-qubit gates in capacitively coupled flopping-mode spin qubits
item.description: Versatile set of quantum gates between qubits of a spin quantum computer node.

item.title: Hybrid superconductor-semiconductor systems for quantum technology
item.description: Perspectives article in Applied Physics Letters special topic Hybrid Quantum Devices. We summarize recent progress and theoretical models that describe superconducting-semiconducting hybrid quantum systems, explain the limitations of these systems, and describe different directions where future experiments and theory are headed.

item.title: Flopping-mode electric dipole spin resonance
item.description: The flopping-mode configuration enables low-power spin control in quantum dot arrays.

item.title: Electric-field control and noise protection of the flopping-mode spin qubit
item.description: The flopping-mode spin qubit can be efficiently controlled and protected from charge fluctuations.

item.title: Optimized cavity-mediated dispersive two-qubit gates between spin qubits
item.description: Performance of single-electron spin qubits in DQDs with respect to dispersive long-distance two-qubit gates mediated by virtual cavity photons.

item.title: A coherent spin–photon interface in silicon
item.description: First demonstration of strong coupling between a single spin in silicon and a single microwave-frequency photon.

item.title: Input-output theory for spin-photon coupling in Si double quantum dots
item.description: The recent advances in Si DQDs fabrication and control, a spin-photon coupling of more than 10 MHz with a sufficiently low spin decoherence rate is achievable, potentially allowing the strong-coupling regime and paving the way towards a spin-based quantum processor with full connectivity.

item.title: Random-walk topological transition revealed via electron counting
item.description: Exploring topological dynamics in a classical stochastic random walk.

item.title: Topologically Enforced Bifurcations in Superconducting Circuits
item.description: Exploring the relationship of topological insulators and superconductors and the field of nonlinear dynamics.

item.title: Full-counting statistics of time-dependent conductors
item.description: Computing the full-counting statistics of transport described by Markovian master equations with an arbitrary time dependence

item.title: Transport, shot noise, and topology in AC-driven dimer arrays
item.description: Interplay of transport, shot noise, and topology in driven QD arrays.

item.title: Dissipative long-range entanglement generation between electronic spins
item.description: Proposal for deterministic generation and long-term stabilization of entanglement between two electronic spin qubits confined in spatially separated quantum dots.

item.title: Topological Instabilities in ac-Driven Bosonic Systems
item.description: Interplay of instability and topology in driven bosonic systems.

item.title: Edge-state blockade of transport in quantum dot arrays
item.description: Novel transport blockade mechanism in quantum dot arrays and conducting molecules based on an interplay of Coulomb repulsion and the formation of edge states.

item.title: Degenerate parametric oscillation in quantum membrane optomechanics
item.description: Degenerate parametric oscillation, one of the most elusive models in the field of open system dynamics, can be implemented in modern optomechanical setups.

item.title: Floquet Majorana fermions in superconducting quantum dots
item.description: We consider different configurations of ac driven quantum dots coupled to superconductor leads where Majorana fermions can exist as collective quasiparticles.

item.title: Floquet engineering of long-range p-wave superconductivity
item.description: Floquet Majorana fermions appear as steady states at the boundary of time-periodic topological phases of matter.
